view: HERO landing composition — the river meeting the Loop, z14.1
shows: The composed landing view: the river, its bridges and the downtown grid in frame, minimal labels, no traffic primitives.

view: Fit city — the active road network filling the viewport
shows: Fit is derived from the street network, so Chicago fills the frame instead of floating as a postage stamp beside the empty lake.
City zoom carries land, water, major parks, highway and arterial structure and a handful of labels — no buildings, no street names, no signals, no vehicles.

view: Neighborhood — the Loop and River North, z14.6
shows: Neighborhood zoom adds the local street network and simplified building mass; labels stay to districts and landmarks.

view: Street zoom in the Loop, z16.6
shows: Street zoom: real building footprints with their own boundary, one label per street, road hierarchy by width rather than colour.

view: Chicago River and its bridges, z15.0
shows: The river reads as the strongest geography on the map; bridge decks keep their own material and the banks are clean of sliver fragments.
The interchange stays legible through carriageway structure, ramps and casing width — and the highways no longer scream orange.

view: Grant Park and the lakefront, z14.6
shows: Park green is quiet and desaturated, with no generated canopy dot field and no tiny grass fragments competing with the lake.
Real footprints at two restrained tones with a light boundary — a map, not a faceted low-poly mesh.
